Two sources (Andrews + P&E via POLLEX) attest the word. pe_via_pollex = match, so the spelling is P&E's. Hawaiian Wikipedia has 7 one-word uses for 'bridge'. gloss_source: Wiktionary; Andrews 1922

adjudication_reason: The word, spelling and gloss are certain: Andrews, Wiktionary, POLLEX (P&E form, match) and Johnson 2008. The sources split on the first morpheme. Andrews and Johnson read au 'time', which is the dossier's only au id (PPN *qau 'current; era'). POLLEX (note: 'Cf. PPN *aqu come, reach, arrive; *mohe sleep') and Wiktionary derive aumoe from PN *aqu-mohe 'fast asleep', and *aqu is not the dossier's au. The cards print each root's ancestor, so linking aumoe's AU to *qau words would contradict its own etymon. The first reader saw this conflict but assigned 'au' anyway, saying it 'affects linking, not inclusion'. Linking is exactly what the sense id is for. And until the root is known, it is not established that aumoe is a compound of exactly these two roots, so keep-pending, not keep.

On top of that, the word is single-source and Andrews calls it the less usual variant of makole, and the gloss is a disease. Degree 18 does not outweigh this.
